description:
Initialize the OTEL tracer provider at startup and add it as a layer on the existing tracing-subscriber stack. Flush spans on shutdown.

## What to do
In main.rs, when config.observability.enabled is true:

  1. Build an OTLP gRPC exporter pointed at config.observability.otlp_endpoint
  2. Build a TracerProvider with a BatchSpanProcessor (not SimpleSpanProcessor — batch is required for production throughput)
  3. Install it as the global tracer via opentelemetry::global::set_tracer_provider(...)
  4. Build a tracing_opentelemetry::layer() and add it to the subscriber stack alongside the existing fmt layer

  The subscriber becomes:
    tracing_subscriber::registry()
      .with(fmt_layer)          // existing human/json fmt output
      .with(otel_layer)         // new: OTLP span export (feature-gated)
      .init();

  5. On shutdown: call opentelemetry::global::shutdown_tracer_provider()
     BEFORE the tokio runtime exits, or in-flight spans are lost.
     Wire into the existing graceful shutdown path in main.rs.

## Why BatchSpanProcessor
SimpleSpanProcessor blocks the calling task on every span export — latency spike on every request. BatchSpanProcessor exports asynchronously with configurable queue size and flush interval.

## Acceptance
- With features=otel and observability.enabled=true, a test request produces an OTLP export call (observable via mock OTLP server or wiremock)
- With features=otel and observability.enabled=false, no OTLP connection is attempted
- cargo test -p stoa-mail passes (OTLP endpoint unreachable must not panic at startup; log warning and continue)
title: Wire OTEL tracer provider and subscriber layer in main.rs
